best_for: RSS readers on Windows or Mac who want a clean desktop app, either on its own or as a front end for a Fever, Google Reader API, Inoreader or Feedbin account.

points.title: Local feeds or your sync service
points.text: It can fetch feeds on its own, or sync with self-hosted services that speak the Fever or Google Reader API. Inoreader, Feedbin, The Old Reader and BazQux Reader are supported too, so the account you already use keeps working.

points.title: Rules sort the flood
points.text: Regex rules can hide, mark as read or star articles as they arrive. Background fetching sends a notification when something new lands.

points.title: Full articles in the app
points.text: A built-in view loads the full article text instead of the feed's teaser, or you can load the original web page. Single-key shortcuts move you through the list.

points.title: Easy to leave
points.text: Subscriptions import and export as OPML, and you can back up and restore all app data. Switching readers later costs little.

points.title: Free under BSD 3-Clause
points.text: Fluent Reader is open source under the BSD 3-Clause license and built with Electron, React and Fluent UI. A mobile version lives in a separate project.

points.title: Windows listing lags behind
points.text: The newest GitHub release is 1.3.2, but the Windows listing here stops at 1.2.2, with 24 versions in x86 and x64 machine-wide installers. The project recommends the Microsoft Store on Windows for automatic updates. macOS lists only the current universal build, marked for macOS 13 or later.
